description: ETHIO COFFEE CLIMATE LAB is developing Coffee Climate Intelligence Ethiopia (CCIE), a project exploring how NASA Earth observation and climate data can reveal temperature, rainfall, and vegetation trends in Ethiopia's coffee-growing regions. We aim to translate satellite and climate data into practical insights for climate-resilient coffee production and sustainable agriculture. We welcome collaborators in GIS, earth science, coding, data analysis, statistics, AI, and visualisation.
summary:
Coffee Climate Intelligence Ethiopia (CCIE), developed by ETHIO COFFEE CLIMATE LAB, is an Earth observation-based project designed to investigate environmental trends affecting Ethiopia's coffee-growing landscapes. Responding to NASA's "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge, CCIE explores how NASA Earth science data can be transformed into practical climate intelligence for agriculture.

The project focuses on three major coffee-producing areas: Sidama, Yirgacheffe, and Jimma. It proposes combining NASA POWER climate data and MODIS satellite-derived vegetation indices to examine temperature, precipitation, and vegetation patterns over time. Through environmental trend analysis, regional comparisons and a proposed interactive dashboard, CCIE aims to make complex Earth observation information easier to understand and apply.

The project addresses the gap between satellite-based environmental information and local agricultural decision-making. Its intended beneficiaries include coffee farmers, researchers, agricultural businesses, investors, and policymakers. By improving access to environmental insights, CCIE aims to support climate adaptation, sustainable coffee production, biodiversity conservation, and climate-informed agricultural investment.

By connecting NASA Earth science with Ethiopia's globally significant coffee sector, CCIE presents a scalable approach to turning environmental observations into actionable sustainability intelligence.
details:
Coffee Climate Intelligence Ethiopia (CCIE)

Turning NASA Earth Observations into Climate Intelligence for Ethiopia's Coffee Landscapes

Team: ETHIO COFFEE CLIMATE LAB
Challenge: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026
Challenge Theme: Be An Earth System Trend Detective!
Geographic Focus: Sidama, Yirgacheffe and Jimma, Ethiopia.

1. Project Overview

Coffee Climate Intelligence Ethiopia (CCIE) is an Earth observation-based project designed to investigate environmental trends affecting Ethiopia's coffee-growing landscapes.

The project explores how NASA Earth science resources can be used to examine changes in temperature, precipitation, and vegetation conditions across three important coffee-producing areas.

CCIE aims to bridge the gap between satellite-based environmental observations and practical agricultural decision-making.

2. The Problem

Ethiopia's coffee production depends on environmental conditions, including rainfall, temperature, vegetation health, and ecosystem stability.

However, environmental datasets are not always accessible or easily interpreted by farmers, researchers, agricultural businesses, and policymakers.

CCIE addresses this information gap by proposing an accessible framework for regional climate and vegetation analysis.

3. Our Approach

The proposed solution consists of four stages:

  1. Data collection: Obtain NASA POWER climate information and MODIS vegetation indicators.
  2. Trend analysis: Investigate temperature, precipitation and vegetation patterns over time.
  3. Regional comparison: Examine environmental patterns across Sidama, Yirgacheffe and Jimma.
  4. Visualization: Translate observations into maps, charts and an interactive climate intelligence dashboard.

4. NASA Earth Science Resources

  • NASA POWER: https://power.larc.nasa.gov/
  • NASA MODIS MOD13Q1: https://ladsweb.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/missions-and-measurements/products/MOD13Q1/
  • NASA Earthdata Search: https://search.earthdata.nasa.gov/

5. Intended Beneficiaries

  • Smallholder coffee farmers
  • Coffee cooperatives and exporters
  • Agricultural researchers
  • Sustainability and development organizations
  • Agricultural investors
  • Government institutions and policymakers

6. Expected Impact

CCIE aims to support:

  • Climate adaptation in coffee-producing landscapes.
  • Environmental risk awareness.
  • Sustainable coffee production.
  • Biodiversity and ecosystem conservation.
  • Climate-informed agricultural investment.
  • Evidence-based regional planning.

7. Technology and Tools

The proposed technical framework includes:

  • NASA POWER
  • MODIS Earth observation data
  • NASA Earthdata
  • Geospatial data visualization
  • Google Earth Engine (proposed for data processing)
  • Microsoft PowerPoint
  • ChatGPT for AI-assisted ideation, research organization and writing.

8. Current Development Status

CCIE is currently at the project concept and analytical framework stage.

The next development phase will focus on obtaining and processing NASA datasets, validating environmental patterns, preparing regional visualizations, and developing an interactive dashboard.

No quantitative environmental trend findings are claimed until the relevant data analysis and validation have been completed.

9. Future Vision

Our long-term vision is to establish a scalable climate intelligence framework that can be extended beyond coffee to other Ethiopian agricultural value chains.

Potential future applications include:

  • Tea
  • Horticulture
  • Enset
  • Cereals
  • Agroforestry
  • Agricultural investment and climate risk assessment

10. Team

ETHIO COFFEE CLIMATE LAB

Project: Coffee Climate Intelligence Ethiopia (CCIE)

Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

AI assistance was used in project ideation, research organization, and writing. Scientific findings must be based on actual NASA observations and appropriate validation.
